question.value: Is there 183 and 380 GHz water maser emission in the 22 GHz gigamaser galaxy TXS 2226-184, and what is its nature (disk vs jet/outflow)?

evidence.quote: To date, the nature of this maser is still being debated, in particular, whether it is associated with a nuclear accretion disk or with an ejection component

findings_qualitative.value: Both lines show two-peaked profiles like the 22 GHz maser and are co-spatial within errors; the 183 and 380 GHz masers have centroid positions coincident within 1 mas.

evidence.loc: 4.2 The possible nature of the maser emission
evidence.quote: the position derived from centroid measurements of both the 183 and 380 GHz masers is coincident, within the statistical uncertainty of 1 mas

claims.hypothesis: TXS 2226 hosts 183 and 380 GHz maser emission
claims.result: Two-peaked broad lines at both frequencies, S/N >= 100, L_iso ~1e4-1e5 Lsun
claims.finding: First 380 GHz maser detection in a known 22 GHz maser galaxy; all three transitions in one object

evidence.quote: the first case where all three transitions are present in the same object

claims.hypothesis: The masers arise from the same nuclear structure as the 22 GHz maser
claims.experiment: Compared profiles and centroid positions with 22 GHz data
claims.result: Similar profiles; positions coincident within errors
claims.finding: Same gas likely; nature favors amplification of nuclear continuum from jet or outflow, but more analysis needed

evidence.quote: favors a nature associated with the amplification of a bright nuclear continuum (from a jet or outflow) through dense and hot gas in front of the nucleus

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Thermal origin cannot be ruled out by Tb alone; would require emitting region >0.03 arcsec (15 pc) at 183 GHz, judged unlikely

evidence.quote: the emitting region has to be $>$ 0.03 arcsec (corresponding to 15 pc)

limitations_admitted.value: Preliminary reduction; GBT and ALMA epochs differ by over ten years, so only qualitative comparison; resolution too coarse for maser spot positions

evidence.quote: we note that only a qualitative comparison is performed here
Unfortunately, the spatial resolution is too coarse to yield detailed position estimates of the different maser emitting regions.

referee_caveats_inferred: Maser nature rests on indirect arguments (profile and position), as Tb limits are low
